AI Impact on the Global Job Market

Risk, Salary & Skills Trend Analysis (2015–2035)

Executive Overview

This report examines AI automation risk, salary dynamics, skill demand, and job survival prospects across the global labor market from 2015 to 2035. Based on analysis of 12,343 records spanning 2015-2035 across 6 countries and 10 job titles, we present data-driven insights for strategic workforce planning.

Distinct Roles

Key Finding #1: AI risk scores have increased steadily from 0.30 in 2015 to 0.51 in 2035, representing a 72.0% increase in automation vulnerability across all job categories.
Key Finding #2: Job survival rates are projected to decline from 91.1% in 2015 to 83.7% by 2035, with entry-level roles showing the most significant vulnerability.
Key Finding #3: Python and AWS-related roles demonstrate the strongest job survival prospects, while Excel-dependent and basic data processing roles face the highest automation risk.
Strategic Alert: Roles in India and Australia show higher average AI risk scores compared to USA and Canada, suggesting these markets may experience more significant workforce disruption requiring targeted reskilling investment.

Strategic Recommendations

1. Prioritize Python & AI/ML Skill Development

Data Basis: Python-based roles show 0.35 AI risk score and 100% survival rate. AI Researcher roles show lowest automation risk (0.15) and highest survival (100%).

Action: Invest in Python programming, machine learning, and deep learning training programs. These skills show the highest demand growth (3.0 points) and strongest correlation with job survival.

2. Accelerate Cloud & DevOps Capability Building

Data Basis: AWS (2.7 demand growth) and Docker (-2.5 demand growth) skills show strong upward trajectory. Cloud Engineers demonstrate favorable survival rates (100%).

Action: Cross-train existing employees in cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization technologies. These roles bridge traditional development and AI-enhanced workflows.

4. Proactively Address Entry-Level Vulnerability

Data Basis: Entry-level positions show the highest average AI risk score (0.40) compared to Senior (0.39). Entry-level workers are most exposed to automation displacement.

Action: Implement mentorship programs pairing entry-level employees with senior staff. Create clear progression pathways that emphasize AI-augmented rather than AI-replaced skillsets.

5. Tailor Geographic Workforce Strategies

Data Basis: India (0.40 risk) and Australia (0.40 risk) show elevated AI risk compared to USA (0.40 risk) and Canada (0.39 risk).

Action: Prioritize reskilling investments in higher-risk regions. Consider geographic diversification of roles to balance automation exposure across portfolio.

6. Monitor Declining Survival Rates in Key Roles

Data Basis: Business Analyst (43% survival) and Data Analyst (56% survival) roles show concerning survival rates. Software Engineer (97%) and Data Scientist (100%) remain more resilient.

Action: Audit workforce composition in at-risk roles. Develop transition pathways to higher-survival roles (AI Researcher, ML Engineer) for affected employees.

Strategic Imperative: The data is clear—AI risk is increasing across all dimensions. Organizations that invest proactively inreskilling, particularly in Python/ML/cloud competencies, will be best positioned to navigate the 2025-2035 transition period successfully.
